To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the synaptic mechanisms of mGluR-dependent LTD change over development from a postsynaptic to presynaptic mechanism.

the mechanisms of synaptic plasticity change over the course the postnatal period, with presynaptic mechanisms being important in the early postnatal period and postsynaptic mechanisms becoming more prominent in later postnatal periods.

mGluR-dependent long-term depression (mGlu-LTD) at CA1 synapses in hippocampal slices undergoes a developmental switch in synaptic mechanism, from a postsynaptic, protein synthesis-dependent mechanism in mature synapses to a presynaptic, protein-synthesis independent mechanism in neonatal synapses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the developmental changes in the synaptic mechanisms underlying long-term synaptic depression in the CA1 area of the hippocampus.
how synaptic function changes over time, and how these changes are reflected in the expression of synaptic plasticity.
the developmental switch in synaptic mechanisms of LTD mediated by group 3 metabotropic glutamate receptor (mGlu) in hippocampal neurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
developmental changes in the synaptic mechanisms for mGluR-dependent LTD would affect synaptic dynamics and perhaps information storage over the course of development.
there is a developmental switch in the mechanisms underlying mGluR-dependent LTD, which may be important for the development of synaptic plasticity and the formation of memory.
the synaptic properties of mGluR-dependent LTD are differentially regulated in neonatal and adult hippocampal CA3-CA1 synapses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mGluR-dependent LTD is expressed by different mechanisms during development.
there are two distinct forms of mGluR-dependent LTD in the developing hippocampal CA 1 region.
the synaptic mechanism for group 1 mGluR-dependent LTD switches from a presynaptic mechanism in neonatal animals to a postsynaptic one in adolescent animals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the synaptic properties of the hippocampus change over the course the first few weeks after birth and this is accompanied by changes in the mechanism of synaptic plasticity.
the developmental switch in mGluR-dependent LTD mechanisms may be a key factor that determines the role of mGluR-mediated synaptic plasticity in the developing brain.
